summary.text: 再 is used chiefly for “again” and “a second time.” Its ancient construction is disputed: proposals interpret it as fish-related, a cord-making tool, or a graph expressing one act yielding two. None is confirmed.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One historical analysis reads the graph as 一 with an abbreviated 冓, expressing one act yielding two; other proposals interpret the ancient graph as fish-related or as a cord-making tool. The evidence does not establish a definitive component analysis.

history.text: The supplied evidence reports oracle-bone forms in fragmentary, unclear contexts and bronze uses for “again/second time” and “two.” It does not establish a direct transition from the oracle-bone contexts to those meanings, or which bronze use came first. A curated small-seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact or proof of graphic development.
Variant forms are documented, but the evidence does not give a complete dated sequence from early graphs to the modern standard shape or support a claim of corruption.

uncertainties.text: The graph’s original referent and the identity and roles of its visible parts remain unresolved. The fish account, cord-tool account, and historical “one act yielding two” explanation are competing analyses; the evidence does not establish any as the origin.
Some Warring States forms include 二 or 口; 二 may contribute “two,” but it may also be decorative. This evidence does not show that 二 is a component in every form.
The earliest documented use and the complete chronology of meanings are unresolved. Absolute dates for the cited bronze examples are not supplied.

senses.text: Bronze inscriptions are reported using 再 for “again” or “a second time.” The source does not establish whether this use preceded the attested sense “two.”
A bronze inscription is reported using 再 for “two.” The evidence does not establish priority between this use and the bronze use “again/second time.”
再 is currently used with the sense “again” or “twice.” The dossier supplies this current gloss but does not establish a full sequence of semantic developments from the early uses.

senses.period: Warring States manuscript; absolute date unresolved
senses.text: A Guodian slip may use 再 to write 在. This proposed whole-sign borrowing would write a different word with a similar-sounding sign; it is not a development of 再’s meaning. The interpretation is explicitly uncertain, and the old sound comparison is not supplied.

limitations.text: Early reported uses do not establish which sense came first, the spoken word’s earliest attestation, or a complete chronology connecting early and current meanings.
The proposed borrowing of 再 for 在 is uncertain, and the supplied evidence does not give the historical readings needed to demonstrate the sound match.

overview.text: 再 commonly means “again” or “a second time.” Its ancient shape is disputed, so no particular modern-looking part can be confidently assigned an original meaning.
